scenes.text: Imagine painting your bedroom walls with a color so vibrant, it literally breathes poison into the air while you sleep.
In the Victorian era, a brilliant shade called Scheele’s Green became an absolute obsession, used in grand dresses, living rooms, and even children's toys.
But when these damp green rooms got warm, toxic mold reacted with the wallpaper's secret ingredient—pure arsenic—releasing invisible, lethal gas into the air.
Even the exiled Napoleon might have been slowly killed by his own green bedroom walls, so would you dare to spend a night in a room like this?
